newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to grow 4-5 pct in 1997 - Malan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to grow 4-5 pct in 1997 - Malan.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan said on Monday that gross domestic product will grow between four and five percent in 1997, against three percent this year.

"This year the economy will grow three percent, and in 1997 we estimate the economy will grow between four and five percent -- 4.5 percent on average," Malan said at a seminar about the business future of the Americas.
He forecast that in the five years between 1993 and 1998, the Brazilian economy would grow around 30 percent.
Malan said Brazil's GDP, currently estimated at around $750 billion, would grow to $1 trillion by the year 2001.
"We are creating conditions to grow at higher but sustained growth rates in the future," he said.
Responding to criticism that the government was not reacting to generalized concern that the economy was overheating, Malan said, "This is a lie, absurd, a mistake."
Malan said the economy grew seven percent in the 1996 third quarter compared against the same period last year, because the government eased credit restrictions.
Regarding the trade and current account deficit, Malan said he was unconcerned about criticism from certain sectors because what was important was how the deficit was being financed.
"What is important is how the deficit is being financed and it is being financed by (foreign) direct investment," Malan said.
He said foreign direct investment so far this year had reached $6.6 billion. He said foreign direct investment would reach $7.5 billion for the whole year.
"This has financed more than 40 percent of the deficit," he said. "There is no reason for panic."
